# Burning Springs Update in December: Map expansion Ohio, The Ghoul, 3 new events, new opponents and much more.

![Burning Springs Update in December: Map expansion Ohio, The Ghoul, 3 new events, new opponents and much more.](/uploads/560_blog-teaser-template.jpg)

![skywalka](/public/avatar_skywalka_fo76_nuka_knights_variant2_square_white-black.png) 

With *Burning Springs*, *Fallout 76* is receiving the largest free update since 2020. From the beginning of **December** (more detailed information about the release will be given in the Fallout Day Stream on October 23rd, 2025) players can enter the adjacent **Ohio** region for the first time, accessible via the newly built **Silver Bridge near Point Pleasant**. Here players can expect a war-torn area with a **desert, deathclaws and raiders** that was heavily inspired by *Fallout 3* and *Fallout: New Vegas*. Ohio has hardly been part of the Fallout lore so far and is now a blank space filled with its own stories. A total of over **20 new locations** and attractions await, comparable in size to regions like Skyline Valley or Savage Divide.

The Burning Springs Update starts **parallel to the new season 2 of the Fallout series** on Prime Video. And in addition to the desert landscape, it brings with it other similarities.

## Map expansion to Ohio

Another highlight are the **dynamic weather effects**: **sandstorms** can occur in Ohio, which impair visibility and even influence ongoing events. This, together with the new **background music** composed specifically for Ohio, adds significantly to the atmosphere of the region.

Firing a nuclear bomb on Ohio also has **special effects**. Although Highway Town is exempt from this, other areas respond by changing flora and fauna. New plant species and their irradiated variants as well as enemies such as **Radhogs** clearly show the effects of a nuclear strike.

## Over 20 new locations

**Highway Town** serves as a new **social meeting point** with the **Last Resort**, where players can accept bounty orders, find teams and join forces for the hunt. The developers compare this hub to Diamond City from *Fallout 4*, but this time in a multiplayer context. However, Highway Town is not completely safe - there are hostile characters there too, which preserves the atmosphere of the wasteland.

## New opponents: RAD-Keiler and the Rust Faction

With *Burning Springs* new enemies appear. Particularly mentioned were the **RAD boars**, which show a striking reaction to nuclear impacts and thus cause additional surprises in the wasteland. The RAD boar can even be tamed as a pet for your CAMP if you dare.

Additionally, the **Rust Faction** has been confirmed - a hostile group led by the Rust King that is making Ohio unsafe. Within this faction, players will also encounter **deathclaws with armor**, which further underline the danger of the new region.

## The ghoul from the Fallout series

You all know the ghoul from the Fallout series played by **Walton Goggins**. This ghoul is now also finding its way into Fallout 76 with *Burning Springs*. In the Fallout series, the ghoul is a bounty hunter, and that is exactly his central task in this update. He offers you a job to help him with his bounty hunts. This is how you meet him for the assignments at the Last Resort in Ohio. The ghoul was even voiced by Walton Goggins himself.

## New bounty hunter system

A central element is the new **bounty system**. There are two levels: **Grunt Hunts**, smaller missions that can be completed alone or in small groups, and **Headhunts**, large-scale public events. The latter are particularly demanding, but also bring unique rewards, a lot of experience and bottle caps. Only one Headhunt runs per server at a time, while Grunt Hunts are unlimited
